section_entries.label: 1. Introduction
section_entries.mathematical_role: Defines the heat-deformed cosine-transform family, relates its zero geometry to RH and the de Bruijn-Newman threshold, represents the family through its zeros, and states the Lehmer-pair lower-bound criterion.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Monotone real-zero flow and the de Bruijn-Newman threshold
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: Combines persistence of real zeros under increasing deformation time with a sharp threshold Λ, identifies RH with Λ at most zero, and explains Newman's opposite inequality as the claim that RH is at the boundary of instability under perturbation.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Lehmer pairs compare a tiny gap with interaction from all other zeros
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: Defines a Lehmer pair by multiplying the squared gap between consecutive simple positive zeros by an interaction sum over every other signed zero. The criterion compresses a global zero configuration into one local-gap-versus-background test.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: Hadamard factorization replaces the entire function by a symmetric, inverse-square-summable zero configuration, exposing the data later interaction estimates actually use.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: For real t, H_t is stated to be an even real entire function of order one and maximal type, with H_t(0)>0. It is represented by a product over factors involving x²/x_j(t)², and the inverse squares of its zeros are summable; at t=0 the positive-side indexing is extended by x_{-j}=-x_j.
directed.conceptual_reading: The factorization compresses analytic-function information into zero locations while evenness removes redundant sign data. Summability is what makes later global interaction sums controllable rather than merely formal.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The Hadamard product bridges an entire function to a discrete point configuration, and the signed indexing bridges even symmetry to sums over all nonzero integer indices.
directed.boundary_or_failure: This representation does not by itself show that the relevant zeros are real or simple, nor does it supply the later Lehmer inequality. Exact product-factor typography is representation-sensitive.
directed.uncertainty: The prose, symmetry convention, and inverse-square convergence are legible; the exact displayed factor should be scan-checked before formula-level reuse.

supported: The span states that H_t is even, real entire of order one and maximal type, displays a Hadamard product with prefactor H_t(0)>0, gives inverse-square summability, and fixes the signed indexing at t=0.
The candidate correctly identifies the zero-set and symmetry representations and warns that realness and simplicity are not established here.
inference: The summable signed zero representation is naturally useful for zero-geometry and later interaction estimates.
unsupported_or_imported: The spontaneous claim that factorization replaces the entire function by a zero configuration, and the directed claim that it compresses the function into zero locations, omit the displayed multiplicative normalization H_t(0); the zeros alone are not the full represented function.
